question: Is the following claim true? Neptune was discovered in 1846.
source: author-written for this project; verified by the author

claims.text: Neptune was first observed on September 23, 1846, by Johann Galle at the Berlin Observatory.
Le Verrier and Adams independently predicted Neptune's position from irregularities in Uranus's orbit.
The 1846 date is well documented and widely cited.
Adams made calculations around 1845, before the 1846 observation.
Adams never published a prediction that led to an observation, so he did not discover Neptune.
Galileo recorded Neptune in 1612-1613 as a fixed star without recognizing it as a planet.
The earlier calculations and sightings do not change the discovery date.
The question concerns when Neptune was discovered, not who first noticed it or when it was first recorded.
The 1846 Galle observation guided by Le Verrier's prediction is the standard historical account of the discovery.
Earlier calculations and sightings were not recognized discoveries at the time, so they do not overturn 1846.
